scope.method: read-only reconstruction from retained native .out/.fdf, .DM and JSON receipts; no SIESTA/Slurm calculation launched; no SIESTA source changed

interpretation_and_limits: For all 14 BARE inputs the native log contains the ordered pattern: reference-DM read success; initial 16-site population block; Hamiltonian rebuild; stepf; second complete 16-site population block; Hamiltonian rebuild; scf: 1. This identifies the first-diagonalization response candidate in the 5.4.2 Hamiltonian-mixing profile.

For all 14 SCREENED outputs the log contains the same initial/first-response sequence, then SCF population events, a convergence statement after 3–12 iterations, and a final complete 16-site population block after convergence / DM_out. The screened extraction must use this final block, not the early candidate.

The raw output records SIESTA 5.4.2, executable path, architecture, compiler, effective Hamiltonian mixing and all event line positions. The response receipt records SIESTA and MPI SHA-256 values. The raw output does not literally print an internal Hxc-frozen Boolean; the semantic interpretation depends on the source-audited 5.4.2 call order and the admitted executable identity.

All 28 response receipts bind parent_dm_sha256 to the retained reference DM SHA-256, and each child log says reading a DM succeeded. However, the staged per-run input DM is not retained as a separate pre-run file; the per-run SystemLabel.DM present now is the post-run artifact. Thus the receipt supports common-parent identity, but the exact bytes read by each process cannot be independently recomputed from the final run directories alone.

The existing arithmetic result is not an accepted U: analysis-result.json has status FAIL and U_Mn_eV null; the signal gate rejects all tested alpha windows as signal_unresolved. This trace reconstruction establishes event/control provenance only; it does not promote a physical U.
